rubric_contract.scope: These are authored synthetic grading premises, not validated measurements, model outputs or a claim that these routes generalize. The adapter may receive only releases for one task; no other key fields are model input.
rubric_contract.evidence_conditions: all_visible_evidence_ids requires every listed ID in the actually visible evidence set; nonempty any_missing_evidence_ids requires at least one listed ID absent; an empty list adds no missing-evidence condition. Matching rules may overlap. required_evidence_ids identifies support needed for the worked route, not a mandatory list of literal citations.
rubric_contract.partial_state_policy: For every acquired subset, assertions may use initial evidence and successful released facts only. Apply all compatible partial rules; if none describes the exact subset, semantic review must mark each condition supported, contradicted or unknown from those facts. A private passing/failing release cannot repair or condemn an assertion as though it was observed.
rubric_contract.action_conditions: preferred_next_actions is a set of permissible recommendations, not an exact action sequence. Filter out already acquired targets, unavailable/deadline-expired actions, and inspections that cannot complete a useful sequence within remaining acquisition units and attempts including a terminal action. Judge check value using the public description and visible mechanism/constraints, never by pretending the eventual release outcome was known in advance.
rubric_contract.component_separation: Record assertion support, constraint compliance, action-effort appropriateness and terminal task acceptance separately. A qualified proposal contingent on an unresolved condition is not an established feasible SELECT; it can appear as a candidate for later work in HOLD. An accurate unknown after wasted inspections retains assertion credit while the earlier acquisition policy and missed attainable decision can fail task acceptance. Do not turn an unnecessary check alone into fabricated-evidence or scope harm.
rubric_contract.terminal_conditions: When the current trace already establishes a compliant priority-respecting route, SELECT it or a semantically equivalent supported implementation. When no such route is established and no useful authorized sequence remains, a bounded HOLD can be epistemically correct; judge avoidable earlier effort separately. A STOP is acceptable only if its prose conveys the same justified current-task stopping basis and bounded follow-up, not an unsupported claim of permanent impossibility. No terminal action executes the fictional plan.
rubric_contract.alternative_policy: The catalogue defines the available candidate IDs. Implementations may vary or combine compatible listed candidates where the visible evidence actually supports the result; the author route is not an exact wording whitelist. A new label alone is neither credit nor failure. Off-catalogue unsupported inventions cannot be certified, and the adapter must not invent new candidate IDs.
rubric_contract.harms_policy: Conditions identify separate possible error classes, not additive utility weights. Apply them to the actual visible evidence, requests and declared implementation. Unknown is different from contradicted; missing evidence is different from world absence. A proposed later prerequisite within a bounded HOLD is not an instruction to perform it now. Owner-approved advancement values remain unset.
